explain.say: Here is a question: what are you good at? If you said "nothing", think again! Everyone has strengths, which are things you do well or that come naturally to you. Look at the board: strengths come in different kinds.

faq.a: Strengths are things you do well or that come naturally to you. They can be skills, like drawing, or parts of your character, like kindness or bravery.

faq.q: Is being kind a real strength?
faq.a: Yes! Kindness, fairness, honesty and bravery are character strengths. They help friendships, teams and families work well, and people value them highly.

faq.q: How do I find my strengths?
faq.a: Notice what you enjoy, what makes time fly, and what people thank you for. Ask a family member, teacher or friend what they think you are good at.
asks: How do I know what I am good at?

faq.q: What if I am not good at anything?
faq.a: Everyone has strengths, even if they are quiet ones like being patient or a good listener. Sometimes others can see them more easily than you can.
asks: I am not good at anything

faq.a: Yes. With practice, almost any skill can grow, and character strengths like patience or bravery grow each time you use them.
asks: Can I get better at things I am bad at?

facts: Psychologists Christopher Peterson and Martin Seligman listed 24 character strengths, such as kindness, bravery, curiosity and humour, valued across many cultures.
In a 2005 study, people who used one of their top strengths in a new way every day for a week felt happier for up to six months.
